beats.say: This white hill in Türkiye isn't *snow*, and it isn't ice.
It was built by *hot water* rising from underground.
The water is about *35 degrees Celsius* and full of calcium.
As it flows, the calcium turns into stone and builds *white terraces*.
These terraces are called *travertines*.
They stretch for about *2.7 kilometers*.
From afar it looks like a castle of cotton: *Pamukkale* means cotton castle.
In 1988 it joined the *UNESCO* list with the ancient city of Hierapolis.
But for years, this white hill was turning *brown*.
In Part 2: the *hotels* built on top of it.
*Follow* so you don't miss it.

publish.title: This Isn't Snow. It's Pamukkale ☁️ Part 1 #shorts
publish.description:
The travertine terraces of Pamukkale in Denizli, Türkiye: white limestone pools built by hot spring water over thousands of years. A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988.

Series: Secrets of Pamukkale & Hierapolis — Part 1/5. Watch all parts on the channel.

beats.say: There used to be *hotels* right on top of Pamukkale.
When tourism boomed, hotels and *roads* went up on the hill.

show.label: HOTELS ON THE HILL
show.ai: 1980s hotels and a paved road built directly on top of the white travertine terraces of Pamukkale, tourists and parked cars, faded color photograph

beats.say: The hot spring water was pumped into hotel *swimming pools*.
Terraces without water dried out and started to turn *dark*.
Reportedly, people even rode *motorbikes* across the terraces.

show.label: MOTORBIKES ON THE POOLS
show.ai: a 1980s motorbike riding across the white travertine pools of Pamukkale, splashing water, faded color photograph

beats.say: The snow-white stone turned *grey and brown*.
After the UNESCO listing, the hotels were *demolished*.
The road over the terraces was *removed* too.
Today you can only walk the terraces *barefoot*.
Water is now sent to the pools in *rotation* to keep them white.
In Part 3: the *Gate to Hell* above the terraces.
*Follow* so you don't miss it.

Hotels on the travertines, spring water diverted into their pools, and the demolition after UNESCO listing: why you now walk Pamukkale barefoot.

beats.say: Right above Pamukkale there's a real *Gate to Hell*.
The ancients called it the *Ploutonion*, the cave of Pluto, god of the underworld.
The geographer *Strabo* wrote that sparrows he threw inside died at once.

show.label: GEOGRAPHER STRABO
show.ai: ancient Greek geographer Strabo in a white himation releasing small sparrows toward a dark misty cave entrance among Roman ruins, early morning

beats.say: Yet the priests walked in and came out *alive*.

show.label: THE PRIESTS SURVIVED
show.ai: tall ancient eunuch priests of Cybele in long robes walking out of a steaming cave entrance at Hierapolis, a sacrificial bull collapsed on the misty ground, dawn light

beats.say: In 2013, Italian archaeologists *rediscovered* the cave.
During the dig, birds flying too close *dropped dead*.

show.label: WHY DID BIRDS DIE?
show.ai: modern archaeologists in a Roman excavation at Hierapolis looking at small dead birds lying on the ground near an ancient stone arch, misty morning

beats.say: The secret: *carbon dioxide* rising from the ground.
Measurements found up to *91 percent* CO2 near the floor.
The gas is heavy and stays low, so tall priests may have *breathed above it*.
Did the priests know the trick? *Comment* below.
In Part 4: *Cleopatra's Pool*. *Follow* so you don't miss it.

beats.say: In this pool, people swim between *ancient columns*.
The columns fell into the water during an *earthquake* in Hierapolis.
The water stays around *36 degrees* all year.
Its famous nickname: *Cleopatra's Pool*.
According to legend, Mark Antony gave it to Cleopatra as a *gift*.

show.label: THE LEGEND
show.ai: Queen Cleopatra bathing in a warm turquoise thermal pool among marble Roman columns, steam rising, golden hour

beats.say: But there's *no evidence* she ever swam here.
Marble column pieces still lie on the *bottom* of the pool.
In ancient times, Hierapolis was already a *healing* city.
People traveled from far away to bathe in its *hot springs*.
And the water still *fizzes* with bubbles today.
In Part 5: one of the *oldest machines* ever drawn.
*Follow* so you don't miss it.

beats.say: A tomb near Pamukkale has a *machine* carved on it.
The necropolis of Hierapolis holds *more than 1,200* tombs.
One belongs to a craftsman named Marcus Aurelius *Ammianos*.
It shows a water-powered *stone-cutting saw*.

show.label: WATER-POWERED STONE SAW
show.ai: reconstruction of a 3rd century Roman water-powered stone sawmill: a large wooden water wheel driving cranks and connecting rods that move two saw blades through marble blocks, Hierapolis

beats.say: It's the earliest known image of a *crank and connecting rod*.
It was carved about *1,700 years* ago, in the 3rd century AD.
Engineering long before the *Industrial Revolution*.
The city's huge *theatre* is still standing.
And the apostle *Philip* is believed to have died here.
